headline: Tax filing deadline extended to July 6
teaser: Flooding in Accra pushed back Q2 CIT, PIT and May VAT/NHIL/CST deadlines — file late and normal penalties resume.
bodyHtml:
Following heavy flooding in Accra, GRA extended the deadline for second-quarter Corporate Income Tax (CIT), Personal Income Tax (PIT), and May VAT/NHIL/CST returns to Monday, July 6, 2026. Returns filed by the revised date won't attract late filing penalties, but normal penalties resume for anything filed after.

What this means for you: If flooding disrupted your operations, this was your relief window. Going forward, GRA is encouraging use of the Taxpayer's Portal to reduce future disruption risk.

Enforcement is active: GRA continues to pursue outstanding tax debts, including recently sealing a company's premises over a multi-million cedi liability — a reminder that historical obligations don't disappear. Staying current avoids painful surprises later.

headline: GIPC is becoming GIPA
teaser: Parliament has passed the GIPA Bill 2026 — lower capital thresholds, annual renewals, and wider expatriate quotas once it's signed into law.
bodyHtml:
Parliament has passed the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) Bill, 2026, which will repeal the GIPC Act (Act 865) once it receives presidential assent. This is one of the most significant regulatory changes for foreign investment in Ghana in over a decade.

Key changes to know:

  • Minimum capital requirements removed for most wholly foreign-owned enterprises and joint ventures (trading companies still face a threshold, though lowered)
  • Annual renewal replaces the previous two-year registration cycle
  • Expatriate quotas expanded up to 12 foreign staff positions for larger investments
  • New investor obligations around sustainability and human rights
  • A 24-hour expedited service for registration, renewal, and certificate reissuance

What this means for you: If you're planning to register a foreign-owned or joint-venture business in Ghana, timing matters. We're tracking presidential assent closely and will guide clients through the transition from GIPC to GIPA as it happens.

headline: Ghana's FDA gaining regional standing
teaser: Germany's Paul-Ehrlich-Institut is backing Ghana's FDA to become a regional hub for blood product regulation across West Africa.
bodyHtml:
Germany's Paul-Ehrlich-Institut has pledged support to help Ghana's FDA become a regional centre of excellence for regulating blood and blood products across West Africa — a signal of growing international confidence in Ghana's regulatory systems.

Ongoing compliance reminders:

  • Alcoholic energy drinks (alcohol + stimulant combinations) were required off the Ghanaian market by end of March 2026. Products remaining after the deadline face regulatory sanctions.
  • Draft advertising guidelines for regulated products are in progress — worth watching if your business markets food, drugs, cosmetics, or medical devices.
